name: Corneal Specular Reflection
description: Analyzes corneal specular reflections for geometric consistency — both eyes should reflect the same scene, and AI-generated faces often fail to produce consistent reflections (Nishino & Nayar, 2004).
mechanism:
This method detects AI-generated or manipulated facial video by analyzing the specular highlights reflected on the corneal surface:

1. **Corneal Highlight Detection and Extraction**: The method first locates the eyes using a face landmark detector and segments the iris/pupil region. Within each eye, corneal specular highlights are identified as bright spots (local intensity maxima above the 95th percentile of the iris region). The shape, position, and intensity of these highlights are extracted using sub-pixel localization. In authentic images, corneal highlights are reflections of light sources and environmental features (windows, screens, overhead lights). Both eyes should reflect the same environment from slightly different viewpoints — the interocular baseline creates a small but predictable parallax.

2. **Binocular Reflection Consistency**: The cornea acts as a convex mirror with a radius of curvature ≈ 7.8 mm (Gullstrand model). Given the known eye positions and gaze direction, the method projects the reflected environment from both corneas and checks for geometric consistency (Nishino & Nayar, 2004). In authentic images: (a) both eyes should show the same number of light source reflections, (b) the relative positions of reflections should be consistent with the interocular distance and gaze direction, (c) the reflection shapes should match (same environmental features reflected). AI-generated faces frequently produce reflections that differ between the two eyes — different numbers of highlights, different shapes, or positions that violate the binocular geometry.

3. **Temporal Reflection Coherence**: In video, corneal reflections should move and change in a manner consistent with the head pose, gaze direction, and environmental lighting. As the head rotates, reflections shift according to the law of reflection on the curved corneal surface. The method tracks reflection positions across frames and verifies that their trajectory is consistent with the estimated head motion. AI-generated video often shows reflections that: (a) remain static despite head movement, (b) flicker or disappear between frames, (c) move in directions inconsistent with head rotation.

4. **Environment Map Reconstruction and Validation**: From the corneal reflections, the method reconstructs a partial environment map — an estimate of the scene lighting around the subject. For each eye, the reflection pattern implies an illumination distribution. The method checks: (a) the reconstructed environment maps from both eyes are consistent (same scene from slightly different viewpoints), (b) the environment map is temporally stable, (c) the light source positions in the reflection match visible light sources in the video background when available. Inconsistencies indicate face manipulation or AI generation where reflections are not physically simulated.
parameters:
Face landmark detector: MediaPipe / dlib
Corneal radius of curvature: 7.8 mm (Gullstrand)
Interocular distance: ~63 mm (average adult)
Highlight detection: local maxima above 95th percentile
Sub-pixel localization: parabolic interpolation
Binocular parallax tolerance: 5%
Temporal tracking window: 10 frames
Minimum eye region size: 20×20 pixels
Minimum image resolution: 720p for reliable analysis
accuracy: 80–88% accuracy detecting AI-generated faces via corneal reflection analysis. Binocular consistency achieves AUC of 0.86 for GAN-generated face detection. Temporal coherence analysis provides F1-score of 0.83 for deepfake video. Environment map consistency adds 4–6% accuracy improvement. Performance depends critically on image resolution — requires clear visibility of corneal reflections.
source: Nishino, K. & Nayar, S. K. (2004). Eyes for Relighting. ACM Transactions on Graphics (SIGGRAPH), 23(3), 704–711.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated face images with inconsistent eye reflections. Deepfake video detection through temporal reflection analysis. Verifying portrait authenticity in identity documents. Forensic analysis of video evidence for manipulation detection.
strengths:
• Corneal reflections obey precise optical laws — strong physical constraint
• Binocular consistency is extremely difficult for AI generators to satisfy
• Works regardless of face manipulation method — face swap, reenactment, generation
• Temporal analysis provides video-specific detection signal
• Environment map reconstruction enables cross-validation with scene context
limitations:
• Requires high resolution (≥ 720p) to resolve corneal reflections
• Subjects wearing glasses or contact lenses alter reflection patterns
• Some eye colors (very dark irises) make highlight detection difficult
• Single-eye visibility (profile views) prevents binocular analysis
• Very recent AI models are beginning to generate more consistent reflections
